# Journal of our project:
## Failed Experiment
We looked at the experiment of the student and observed this mistakes:
1. Five data points are not enough to satisfy the Central Limit Theorem (>=30)
2. Array sizes were chosen strictly as powers of ten: 100, 1,000, 10,000, 100,000, and 1,000,000.The difference between 100k and 1mil is to big, he should have choosen steps that were smaller and more useful.
3.Claiming a crossover point at 400,000 elements is an unsupported guess rather than an empirically measured finding.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)
```
## Our process 
We did 2 benchmarks:
First one is similar with the experiment of the student, but we choose more precise steps(100 1000 10000 50000 100000 250000 500000 1000000 2000000) with 30 repetitions.We also randomized it to avoid bias.We get the results in a csv.
Second one is the same, but from 1mil to 20 mil(1000000 2000000 5000000 7500000 10000000 15000000 20000000)
We start with the first one
```{r}
target_csv <- file.path("data", "measurements_mircea-1.csv")
cat("Loading data from:", target_csv, "\n")

df <- read.csv(target_csv, strip.white = TRUE)
df$Type <- factor(df$Type, levels = c("Sequential", "Parallel", "Built-in"))
```
We compute the 95% Confidence Interval 

```{r}
df_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(Size, Type) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean = mean(Time),
    SD = sd(Time),
    SE = SD / sqrt(N),
    CI_lower = Mean - qt(0.975, df = N - 1) * SE,
    CI_upper = Mean + qt(0.975, df = N - 1) * SE,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

We then plot it
```{r}
p <- ggplot(df_summary, aes(x = Size, y = Mean, color = Type, fill = Type)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = CI_lower, ymax = CI_upper), alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = unique(df_summary$Size), labels = label_comma()) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "95% confidence intervals (30 randomized repetitions)",
    x = "Array Size N ",
    y = "Execution Time in Seconds",
    color = "Algorithm",
    fill = "Algorithm"
  ) +theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

print(p)
ggsave("quicksort_benchmark_plot.png", p, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```
We have some observations:
1.At the beginning (100 to 50,000): Parallel is significantly slower than sequential because creating threads takes extra startup time (0.01 vs 0.0001).
2.In the middle (250,000 to 500,000): Parallel catches up to sequential and meets it around 500,000 elements as the data size grows.
3.At the end (1,000,000 to 2,000,000): Parallel gets slower again because spawning over 2,000 threads (THREAD_LEVEL 10) overloads the CPU cores(We changed for the Experiment 2 to THREAD_LEVEL 3).

Experiment 2
The start is the same
```{r}
target_csv <- file.path("data", "measurements_large_mircea.csv")
cat("Loading data from:", target_csv, "\n")

df <- read.csv(target_csv, strip.white = TRUE)
df$Type <- factor(df$Type, levels = c("Sequential", "Parallel", "Built-in"))
```

```{r}
df_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(Size, Type) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean = mean(Time),
    SD = sd(Time),
    SE = SD / sqrt(N),
    CI_lower = Mean - qt(0.975, df = N - 1) * SE,
    CI_upper = Mean + qt(0.975, df = N - 1) * SE,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
p2 <- ggplot(df_summary, aes(x = Size, y = Mean, color = Type, fill = Type)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = CI_lower, ymax = CI_upper), alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = unique(df_summary$Size),
    labels = label_comma()
  ) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "95% confidence intervals for larger sizes (30 randomized repetitions)",
    x = "Array Size N",
    y = "Execution Time in Seconds",
    color = "Algorithm",
    fill = "Algorithm"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

print(p2)
ggsave("quicksort_large_scale_plot.png", p2, width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
```
These are our observations:
1.At the start (1,000,000 to 2,000,000): Parallel (blue) crosses below sequential (red) around 2,500,000 elements.
2.At large scale (5,000,000 to 20,000,000): Parallel stays consistently faster (lower line) than both single-threaded sequential and built-in sorting.
3.Built-in qsort: Becomes the slowest algorithm of all three past 5,000,000 elements.

We next did the extrapolation for larger scale
```{r}
df_model_data <- df %>%
  filter(Size >= 500000) %>%
  mutate(Complexity = Size * log2(Size))
```

```{r}
fit_seq  <- lm(Time ~ Complexity, data = filter(df_model_data, Type == "Sequential"))
fit_par  <- lm(Time ~ Complexity, data = filter(df_model_data, Type == "Parallel"))
fit_libc <- lm(Time ~ Complexity, data = filter(df_model_data, Type == "Built-in"))
```

```{r}
extrap_sizes <- c(unique(df$Size), 30000000, 50000000)
grid_extrap  <- expand.grid(Size = extrap_sizes) %>%
  mutate(Complexity = Size * log2(Size))
```

```{r}
pred_seq  <- data.frame(Size = grid_extrap$Size, Type = "Sequential", Time_Pred = predict(fit_seq, grid_extrap))
pred_par  <- data.frame(Size = grid_extrap$Size, Type = "Parallel",   Time_Pred = predict(fit_par, grid_extrap))
pred_libc <- data.frame(Size = grid_extrap$Size, Type = "Built-in",   Time_Pred = predict(fit_libc, grid_extrap))

df_extrap <- bind_rows(pred_seq, pred_par, pred_libc) %>%
  mutate(Type = factor(Type, levels = c("Sequential", "Parallel", "Built-in")))
```

```{r}
p_extrap <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = df_extrap, aes(x = Size, y = Time_Pred, color = Type), 
            linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = df_summary, aes(x = Size, y = Mean, color = Type), 
            linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = df_summary, aes(x = Size, y = Mean, color = Type), 
             size = 2.5) +
  geom_ribbon(data = df_summary, aes(x = Size, ymin = CI_lower, ymax = CI_upper, fill = Type), 
              alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma(), breaks = c(1000, 100000, 1000000, 10000000, 50000000)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "Quicksort Scaling & Performance Extrapolation (up to N = 50M)",
    x = "Array Size N ",
    y = "Execution Time in Seconds ",
    color = "Algorithm",
    fill = "Algorithm"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

print(p_extrap)
ggsave("quicksort_extrapolation_plot.png", p_extrap, width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)

```
